content.text: Adults = tx of coagulopathy w/ vitamin K supplementation; 10mg dose
Newborns = prophylactic administration of parenteral vitamin K
: vWF-containing factor VIII product (DDAVP usually ineffective in type 2; contraindicated in 2B)
: administered w/ in addition to vWF concentrates or DDVAP to suppress fibrinolysis
: 0.3 μg/kg infused over 20 min increases factor VIII levels 2- to 3-fold in most, but not all, mild-to-moderate hemophilia A patients
Required for bleeding in the gums, GIT, & during oral surgery
Tx w/ factor VIIa or porcine factor VIII
After acute bleeding is controlled → tx w/
Recombinate, Advate, Kogenate FS, Elocate, Adynovate
Tx in those who have factor VIII inhibitors
: coagulation factor IX (recombinant), Fc fusion protein
For control/prevention of bleeding episodes & to manage perioperative bleeding during surgical procedures

: coagulation factor X (human) – 1st and only specific factor X replacement therapy for hereditary factor X deficiency in patients ≥12yo for on-demand treatment and control of bleeding episodes and for perioperative management
: saturates the Fc receptors on mononuclear cells and decreases destruction of opsonized platelets by macrophages
: alternate to IVIG; immunosuppressive that decreases autoantibody production
TPO receptor agonist for pts w/ chronic liver disease prior to undergoing a procedure:
Specific direct thrombin inhibitor therapy for short-term anticoagulation (until platelet count returns to normal & warfarin can be started)
: a vWF-directed antibody fragment for treatment of adults with acquired TTP (aTTP), in combination with plasma exchange and immunosuppressive therapy; recombinant DNA product
: unstable CAD (increased risk of thrombotic events)
: mild cutaneous vasodilation, facial flushing, tachycardia, HA, potential for dilutional hyponatremia
